It is contended by respondent Insurance Company that the petitioner has admitted in his cross- examination that he is one of the two directors of respondent no.2/owner of the vehicle in question.
Respondent no.3 was employee of respondent no.2 company.

sentences.text: The claim of the petitioner cannot be rejected solely on the ground that he has not lodged FIR against respondent no.3 for the offences punishable under Section 279/338 IPC.
10.1(b) This Tribunal has given thoughtful consideration to the contentions of both side.
It is not in dispute that insurance policy of vehicle in question was a comprehensive policy.
It covers the liability qua injuries and death of the occupants of vehicle in question.

As far as the question of non-registration of FIR against respondent no.3 is concerned, it is settled preposition of law that it is not imperative to lodge FIR before maintaining a claim under Motor Vehicles Act for compensation.

This means that the tribunal should consider and  decide with reference to the evidence: (i) whether the  disablement is permanent or temporary; (ii) if the disablement is  permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or  permanent partial disablement, (iii) if the disablement  percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb, then  the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of  the entire body, that is the permanent disability suffered by the  person. If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent  disability then there is no question of proceeding further and  determining the loss of future earning capacity.
After the Tribunal ascertains the  actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on  the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such  permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning  capacity.
The  third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally  disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in  spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still  effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was  earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or  restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions,
